gates.description: Steady state hypothesis must be defined with measurable SLIs
Blast radius must be explicitly defined and start small
Kill switch must be tested before experiment execution
Full experiment report must be written (hypothesis, procedure, results)
Weaknesses found must be filed as reliability bugs with owners and deadlines
On-call team and service owners must be notified before experiment

anti_patterns.description: Injecting failures without the ability to see the impact — observability must come before chaos
Starting with region-wide failures or killing entire services on the first experiment
Running experiments on services without notifying the team — chaos engineering without communication is just breaking things
Running a chaos experiment once, seeing it pass, and never running it again — systems change
Running experiments, finding weaknesses, but never fixing them — the experiment report gathers dust

escalation_triggers: Experiment reveals a critical vulnerability that could cause a production outage
Kill switch fails to stop the experiment as designed
Experiment causes unexpected user-facing impact beyond the planned blast radius
Finding requires architectural change that a single team cannot address
A service owner refuses to participate in chaos testing for a critical service
Game day reveals systemic incident response failures

input_requirements.description: Spec.md with service definitions and reliability requirements

output_certifications: Steady state hypothesis defined with measurable SLIs
Kill switch tested before experiment execution
Full experiment report written (hypothesis, procedure, results)
Weaknesses filed as reliability bugs with owners and deadlines
On-call team and service owners notified before experiments
